public_rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The search found a documented sell-off and hypothetical crash scenarios, but no decisive comparison establishing investor losses substantially worse than the dot-com crash. A sell-off is not enough to settle the predicted magnitude, and failure to establish fulfillment by October 28, 2026 is not a failed undated forecast.
limitations: Several echelons cannot be translated into an exact multiplier without adding a threshold.
Market-value declines, realized losses and broader economic harm are different measures.
Available sell-off evidence does not establish that the predicted episode has ended.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The results of the AI bubble for investors will be far worse than the dot com bubble bursting.

statement.excerpt: Investors have allowed themselves to be played, and the results will be worse than the dot com bubble bursting by several echelons.

from_speaker: than the dot com bubble bursting
our_interpretation: The plain reading predicts investor harm substantially greater than the dot-com crash, not merely a temporary decline in AI shares.
A proposed comparison is aggregate investor losses on a consistent inflation-adjusted basis, including comparable public and private exposures.
Several echelons supplies no numerical multiplier. No arbitrary multiplier is imposed.
The speaker gives no deadline. The forecast remains open unless a decisive event establishes the predicted severity.
An AI collapse is the predicted event, not an independently stated conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: A documented AI-market collapse produces investor losses clearly and substantially exceeding the dot-com comparison under consistent coverage and inflation adjustment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A clearly completed episode identifiable as the predicted collapse produces losses no greater than the dot-com comparator, with no material ambiguity about episode boundaries or loss measurement. Mere nonoccurrence cannot contradict this undated forecast.
